The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services has listed 11 categories of foreign applicants who are exempt from paying the filing fee when submitting Form I-485, the Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, commonly known as a green card application. For most applicants aged 14 and above, according to a Wednesday report by MSN, a Microsoft web portal, the standard fee is 1,390 (approximately KSh180,700) for online filing. However, according to the USCIS fee schedule published in Form G-1055, specific groups are entirely exempt from the charge. The following applicants pay no fee when filing Form I-485: Applicants who served honourably on active duty in the US armed forces and are filing under INA Section 101(a)(27)(K), also known as the Six and Six programme. This exemption does not cover non-military derivative spouses or children. Refugees or those who were paroled as refugees, filing under INA Section 207. Applicants in deportation, exclusion or removal proceedings before an immigration judge, where the court waives the application fee. Persons seeking or granted Special Immigrant Juvenile classification. U nonimmigrants seeking adjustment of status under INA Section 245(m) as victims of qualifying criminal activity. T nonimmigrants seeking adjustment of status under INA Section 245(l) as victims of human trafficking. Persons seeking or granted special immigrant visas or status as Afghan or Iraqi translators or interpreters; Iraqi nationals employed by or on behalf of the US government; Afghan nationals employed by or on behalf of the US government or the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF); or derivative beneficiaries of any of the above. Afghan diplomats or immediate family members who held valid A or G status on July 14, 2021, filing under Section 13 of Public Law 85-316. Persons seeking adjustment of status as abused spouses or children under the Cuban Adjustment Act (CAA). Persons seeking adjustment of status as abused spouses or children under the Haitian Refugee Immigration Fairness Act (HRIFA). Persons seeking immigrant classification as Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) self-petitioners, including derivatives. Beyond the 11 categories that automatically qualify for an exemption, USCIS says certain other applicants may qualify for a fee waiver by submitting Form I-912. Most applicants must still pay the applicable Form I-485 filing fee unless they meet an exemption or receive an approved fee waiver.
